newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. deplores Iraqi interference with its 'copters.
newsitem.headline: U.N. deplores Iraqi interference with its 'copters.

text.p: The Security Council on Friday deplored what it called unacceptable interference by Iraq with the flight of U.N. helicopters working with weapons inspection teams and told Baghdad to take immediate steps to halt such actions.

The statement, read at a brief council meeting, was a followup to a complaint by chief U.N. arms inspector Rolf Ekeus about "four serious incidents" last week in which Iraqi personnel aboard the U.N. helicopters, or Iraqi helicopters flying nearby, had endangered the U.N. craft and their crews .

He said that in one incident, on June 4, an Iraqi shut off the fuel pump of a U.N. helicopter and physically manhandled the air crew chief and a photographer to prevent them from taking photographs of an inspection site, including the departure from the site of two Iraqi helicopters.

The U.N. flights, using helicopters loaned by Chile and manned by Chilean crews, are to ensure that nothing is removed surreptitiously from sites being inspected by ground teams from the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.

The council statement did not deal with a later complaint lodged by Ekeus that Iraq had blocked U.N. teams from two suspected military sites on Thursday and a third location on Wednesday. He said those incidents, involving Iraqi officials who said they were acting on the highest authority, appeared to indicate the Iraqi government had taken a decision to prevent UNSCOM from carrying out its mandate.
The council is expected to deal with those incidents after being briefed by Ekeus next week, and council sources said a formal resolution was likely to be adopted, instead of only a statement.

Friday's statement expressed "serious concern at the four incidents on June 4, 5 and 7, 1997, in which Iraqi personnel unacceptably interfered with helicopter flights operating in support of inspection of sites designated by the Special Commission under Security Council resolutions ... endangering the helicopters and their crews, as well as persons on the ground."
"The Security Council deplores these incidents and underlines that Iraq must immediately take effective steps to put an end to all such actions," the statement added.

It stressed that Iraq was obliged to ensure the safety of UNSCOM personnel and to permit the commission to "carry out its air operations anywhere in Iraq without interference of anykind," in accordance with a resolution adopted soon after the end of the 1991 Gulf war.
